alex: Pushed a sirocco-12B int4 build to staging and ran the long-context sweep (8k -> 32k). Seeing a reproducible token-index translation around the 16k boundary, looks like outputs shift by ~1 token after that point :eyes:

rachel: Ugh. Can you paste the minimal repro and the quant config? Is this only on int4 or also on fp16?

alex: Repro command below. Happens on repeated prompts, including a simple repeating alphabet pattern.

```bash
# repro (run in staging env)
python bench_longctx.py --model sirocco-12B-int4 --quant backend=int4n --max_ctx 32768 --prompt-file tests/long_alpha.txt --dump-debug kv_index,dump_output
```

Config excerpt: kernel_pack: compact_int4, rotary_scale: auto, kv_handshake: enable

ton y: Quick glance at the debug dump, the KV handshake base offset flips when token_pos >= 16384. snippet: 

```
\nDEBUG: kv_index_base=16382
DEBUG: kv_index_base=16383
DEBUG: kv_index_base=0    <-- expected continued indexing, not reset
```

tony: Suspect RoPE index mapping and the int4 packing reshape touching the index math. If fp16 was fine that points at a quant-layout bug.

mei: Can you run the exact same warmup with sirocco-12B-fp16 and post logs? Also try disabling kernel_pack to isolate the pack->index interaction.

alex: Ran fp16 now. No token shift, kv_index_base increments monotonically across boundary. So quant path looks implicated. Disabling kernel_pack (fall back to generic unpack) also removes the shift.

ciara: I grabbed a small diff from the int4 packing code; looks like the reshape in pack_tokens_for_kv() uses floor_div on token groups and underflow at multiples of 16384 gets a stray modulo. Possible off-by-one when combined with rotary tile size.

alex: Posting the tiny debug patch we used to surface the condition:

```python
# debug added in pack_tokens_for_kv()
if token_pos % 16384 == 0 and token_pos > 0:\n    logger.info(f\"pack boundary hit token_pos={token_pos} group_index={group_index} reshape={reshape_shape}\")\n```

deploy-bot: Deployment sirocco-12B-int4 -> staging (build 2025-03-19T12:34Z) succeeded :white_check_mark:

tony: Hypothesis: the int4 stride packing computes group_index = (token_pos >> 3) % tile_width but previously the modulus was applied before adding the chunk offset; with a reshape reorder that can wrap the base unexpectedly when token_pos hits a power-of-two boundary.

rachel: Good hypothesis. Tony, can you prepare a unit test that reproduces the wrap in isolation (no runtime env)? If we can get a tiny python test that fails deterministically we can ship a fix fast.

tony: On it. Preliminary test outline: generate token_pos sequence 0..32768, run pack_tokens_for_kv() with int4 layout and assert monotonic kv_index_base. Will push draft in ~1h.

mei: Also add a regression eval: run a 1k sample of long-context gold prompts with the quant build and compute token-aligned BLEU-like metric and continuity error rate. We need numbers for SRE/SEV doc.

alex: Quick metrics from initial run: continuity_error_rate int4=0.023, fp16=0.0001. Perplexity delta minimal, so this is an alignment issue not model collapse.

ciara: If unit test confirms reshape ordering bug, workaround for customers is to set runtime.kv_alignment = 4096 (forces windowed index base). Will open an operator advisory.

rachel: I'll own the ticket. Created ENG-ML-7891 with steps, logs and suggested patch. Assigning to tony for patch + ciara for QA verification.

alex: Thanks all — priority P1 for staging and recommended hotfix to dedicated pools with heavy long-context traffic.

ciara: QA note: add a fuzz harness for odd boundaries (e.g., 4095,4096,4097,8191,8192,8193,16383,16384,16385) to our nightly longctx suite.

deploy-bot: ENG-ML-7891 created by rachel -> https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/ENG-ML-7891

rachel: tagging @platform-team to consider adding a runtime guard that rejects int4 kernel_pack+auto-rotary unless validated.

alex: I'll follow up with a short writeup for the release notes with the recommended temporary runtime knob.

mei: reminder — include the evaluation harness code path used to compute continuity_error_rate in the ticket so CS can reproduce customer reports.

alex: will do. Closing loop here for now, will post patch link when ready. :thumbsup:
